report.limit: At q=1000 TcpCubic, UDP saturates l1 (E3 l1_util=1.0, l1_drops=911606) and FIFO tail drops leave only about five 1448-byte TCP segments acknowledged over 10 s; RTO backoff and phase/integer accounting cap goodput at 5792 bps (E3, E6, E7, T38, T39, C3, C6, C7).
report.explanation: UDP at 2 Gbps over a 1 Gbps FIFO link keeps the queue full, so most TCP segments are tail-dropped and TCP repeatedly enters RTO backoff. Queue length and TCP type only change the rare phase in which a few segments find queue space and are acknowledged; the delivered payload is therefore an integer-segment effect, not a bandwidth-sharing effect. The best observed value is 5792 bps, tied by TcpCubic at q=1000 and q=250 and by TcpLinuxReno at q=1000, and no tested setting exceeds it by more than 1%.

claims.text: The best observed TCP goodput is 5792 bps, achieved by TcpCubic at q=1000 and q=250 and by TcpLinuxReno at q=1000; no tested setting exceeds it by more than 1%.
The cap is caused by UDP saturation and FIFO tail drops, not by TCP's ability to fill the pipe; r002 had 94120 bytes in flight but only 5792 bps delivered.
Queue length changes phase/integer segment accounting: q500 and q750 deliver one segment, while q250 and q1000 deliver five.
The 31.451 ms RTT in r002 is a stored TCP estimate, not current reverse traffic, because it is constant while forward wait max is 11.441 ms and reverse utilization is zero.
